children: U.S. President Donald Trump announced $500 refunds to nearly 1M Americans enrolled in Obamacare plans across 30 states, with payments set to begin in October, the White House said Thursday.

Obamacare plans, created by Democratic President Barack Obama's signature Affordable Care Act, offer subsidies based on income. The refunds will primarily go to enrollees who do not receive federal premium assistance, including those earning more than 400% of the federal poverty level.
Some people earning between 100% and 400% of the federal poverty level who did not receive subsidies will also qualify. The White House said it has already identified eligible recipients.
The refunds apply to people enrolled through HealthCare.gov in 30 states. They will not cover states that operate their own ACA exchanges, including California and New York.

The refunds will return excess fees collected from insurers on the federal exchange, which are passed on to consumers through premiums. The fee was 1.5% of premiums in 2025 and rose to 2.5% in 2026 before being cut to 1.9% for 2027.
